To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the human pyruate dehydrogenae complex (PDC) is regulated by phosphorylation of its E1p subunit, which inactivates this enzyme.

the human pyruvae dehydrogenase is regulated by phosphorylation of three residues, and that phosphorylation at the first site causes the disordering of the phosphorylation loops that is essential for the inactivation of the pyruvate complex.

the disordering of phosphorylation loops of the pyruvate decarboxylase component of the human PDC by a phosphorylation at site 1 prevents the binding of lipyl domains of the P DC core and thereby inactivates the P DC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis for the inactivation of the PDC by phosphorylation.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of human PDC inactivation and reactivation.
the elucidation of the structural and functional consequences of phosphorylation at the three sites of human E1p.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the disorder of the phosphorylation loops of the phosphorylated E1p is caused by a steric clash between a phosphoryl group and a nearby Ser.

the phosphorylation-induced disruption of the substrate channels and the consequent loss of the reductive acetyl transfer are the key factors responsible for the inactivation of the PDC by the pyruvate kinase-mediated phosphorylation.
the phosphorylation of site 1 of the human E1p protein is sufficient to induce the complete inactivation of the PDC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the disordering of phosphorylation loops by phosphorylation at Ser-264-alpha of E1p is the structural basis of the inactivation of PDC.
phosphorylation-induced disordering of the phosphorylation loops is a key regulatory mechanism for the inactivation of the PDC by phosphorylation.
the disordering of the phosphorylation loops is the molecular basis for the inactivation of the PDC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the disordering of the phosphorylation loops is a general feature of the phosphorylated E1p and is not specific to a particular kinase or the PDC environment.
phosphorylation of E1p at Ser264-alpha is a key regulatory mechanism in the control of human PDC.

the human pyruate dehydrogenae complex (PDC) is a unique enzyme in which the phosphorylation of the catalytic component (E1) is a regulatory mechanism that is used to control the flux through this metabolic pathway.
